result:
PLAT-103 is live: `validateApp` now rejects apps without an `owner`, and all three apps pass theirs. PR #1 passed CI, merged, and CD succeeded. I also built all three apps locally and they compile.

- **Shared contract:** `validateApp` throws `app.owner is required` when `owner` is missing, empty or whitespace. I bumped `libs/shared-contracts` from 1.0.0 to 2.0.0, since this is a breaking change.
- **Apps:** each app takes its owner from the `team` field in its `package.json`: core-shell passes `platform`, billing passes `payments`, and reports passes `insights`.

I shipped all four sub-tasks as one PR instead of the four the ticket lists. `libs/shared-contracts` lives in the monorepo and is inlined into each app at build time, so there's no registry release and no dependency to adopt. One PR also means no app breaks between the library change and its consumers.

I didn't run the apps in a browser, so "still starts up" rests on the builds compiling and the contract check passing.

The ticket called the library change a "shared configuration release", which didn't match how this repo works. The CD docs only mention core-shell and billing as deployed, so I can't tell whether reports actually reaches production.
